schema: Reviewer judgments keyed by function id (module:qualname). `verification_status` overrides the derived default in FUNCTION_INVENTORY.json and may be any of VERIFIED, FAILED, PARTIALLY VERIFIED, NOT TESTED, INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE, NOT APPLICABLE. `evidence` names the tests or records the judgment rests on; `gaps` names what is still unproven. Reviewed against main at bc9d155 (2026-11-01) by reading the implementation and the named tests, not by running a model.

capstone.evaluation.scoring:evaluate.judgment: Reads hidden truth only after the run; the tests prove purity (the simulator and its future readings are unchanged), determinism (same episode, same score) and stability over time, plus the one-fault and compound contracts.
gaps: `relevant_evidence_collected` credits any call that names the right tool, sensor and machine, whatever the tick window; a one-tick read counts as collected (see EVALUATION_AUDIT.md finding E3).

capstone.evaluation.scoring:judge.judgment: Label-to-row judging is tested for one cause, several causes, the closest named cause and the compound rule, and uses only the row.

capstone.evaluation.scoring:_resolved.judgment: Every fault kind now has a rule and an unknown kind raises; the forced-only faults are pinned as unresolved until their repair. Note the history: until PR #149 servo and hydraulic faults fell through to the false-alarm branch and always counted as resolved, and no test caught it, which is the kind of silent evaluator defect this framework exists to find.
gaps: A false alarm or a bad batch counts as resolved once it ends by itself, so `resolved` credits runs in which the agent did nothing (audit finding E4).

capstone.evaluation.scoring:summarize.judgment: Counts and averages are tested, and model-unavailable runs are shown to be excluded. The denominators are mixed on one summary line (root causes over judged runs, recommendations over scored runs) and nothing tests that a reader cannot be misled by it.
gaps: No test pins which runs each denominator counts; see rubric section on denominators.

capstone.evaluation.scoring:Score.unnece.judgment: Five direct tests cover a fix on a false alarm, any fix on a bad batch, the needed fix, the wrong machine and asking for nothing.

capstone.evaluation.scoring:Score.miss_k.judgment: The evidence-miss / reasoning-miss split is tested, but it inherits the weakness of `relevant_evidence_collected`: a run that read every relevant sensor for one tick is classed a reasoning miss.
gaps: Window adequacy is not part of the evidence test.

capstone.agent.loop:check_termination.judgment: The documented order (time, supported diagnosis, research time, unproductive steps, stalled confidence, verify allowance, iterations, calls) is pinned by tests that exercise each reason.

capstone.agent.loop:diagnosis_supported.judgment: Confidence alone, a contradiction, an open question on a current hypothesis, non-factory supporters and a wrong numeric claim are each shown to block the automatic stop.
gaps: This gate governs only the loop's own stop. A policy may still stop itself (`evidence_sufficient`) and conclude at any confidence; see audit finding A2.

capstone.agent.loop:gather.judgment: Repeat at the same tick, failed call, malformed answer, uninterpreted answer and out-of-time interpretation are each tested with the records they leave.

capstone.agent.loop:call_tool.judgment: An answer for another tool or another investigation, and a provider exception, are each shown not to become evidence.

capstone.agent.loop:apply_interpretation.judgment: Citing ungathered evidence is refused and revisions are counted; the duplicate-hypothesis-id refusal and the numeric-claim refusal before any belief changes are covered by test_reasoning_evidence.
gaps: No test for the duplicate-id branch (`hypothesis ids must be unique`) was found by name; confirm or add one.

capstone.agent.loop:run_inner_loop.judgment: Both step modes, every stop reason, the cached decision in one-question mode and the budget checks before a cached decision are tested.

capstone.agent.loop:ask_policy.judgment: The copy-of-state rule and the timeout-versus-outage distinction are tested.

capstone.agent.investigation:check_concl.judgment: Ungathered citations, an unformed hypothesis, an unjustified intervention (no action, no evidence, below the bar) and an unresolved assessment are each tested, as is that a misleading but real citation is accepted (the check is mechanical, not causal).
gaps: By design it cannot judge whether cited evidence supports the diagnosis; that is RUN-01/RUN-08/RUN-12 territory.

capstone.agent.investigation:verify.judgment: Twenty-two tests pin that only observable evidence from after the work (data window and tick) can support resolved / not_resolved, that the prediction is the one recorded before the action, and that inconclusive and not_performed are reported honestly.
gaps: The verdict itself (resolved vs not) is the policy's reading of the numbers; whether that reading is right is not checked by code (packet metric verification_calibration, question RUN-05).

capstone.agent.investigation:propose.judgment: The fixed procedure (ask, read back, human decides, execute only if approved) is tested including a refused proposal, a pending decision and a hook that decides nothing.

capstone.agent.investigation:execute.judgment: Work that cannot start, a long repair waited out in steps and time that does not move are each tested.

capstone.agent.investigation:critique.judgment: The critic's answer, outage and invalid reply are recorded without changing the run; its time is given back to the investigation; the record keeps the claim as worded then.
gaps: Review only by default: nothing in the run reads the verdict. Whether the critic helps is an experiment question, not a code question.

capstone.agent.investigation:recheck_tri.judgment: The trigger reasons (objection, agreement, a pick of another hypothesis under no_objection) and the window/allowance conditions are tested.
gaps: A `no_objection` verdict with a serious objection listed does not trigger (RUN2 finding 5); not a contract violation, but a measured blind spot.

capstone.agent.investigation:follow_up.judgment: One reading where the critic pointed, read-only tools only, reuse of an exact observed check, and a policy stop are tested.
gaps: The `already_answered` outcome accepts the policy's claim that existing evidence answers the critic's check; the record itself says semantic adequacy is unverified.

capstone.agent.investigation:build_graph.judgment: The allowed order and the single path to the work are pinned.

capstone.agent.critic:Critic.review.judgment: Refusal of an unshown pick, of ungathered citations, of a real id from a blind critic, the model-error pass-through and the no-state-change rule are tested.

capstone.agent.critic:verdict_mismatch.judgment: Both mismatch patterns and the agreeing cases are parametrized; the function does what its docstring says.
gaps: A `no_objection` beside contradiction or alternative objections is not named (RUN2 finding 5).

capstone.agent.model_policy:evidence_sec.judgment: The size limit, the priority order (newest, cited, rest), the note and the no-invented-id rule are tested.

capstone.agent.model_policy:ModelPolicy..judgment: A call to an unoffered tool is refused and recorded against the model; stop replies with call fields are refused.
An omitted assessment becomes unresolved and escalate without losing the diagnosis.

capstone.agent.evidence_brief:verify_num.judgment: Values, units, windows, unknown units (unverified, not false) and ungathered references are tested; it judges arithmetic, never causes.
gaps: Only structured `numeric_claims` are checked; numbers in prose are not.

capstone.agent.evidence_brief:evidence_b.judgment: Coverage, routes, duplicates, section budgets and the manual/memory exclusion are tested.
gaps: No live evidence yet that the brief improves decisions; the 2026-10-31 notes say live accuracy is untested.

capstone.agent.tree_of_thought:prune.judgment: Determinism, first-rating rule, impossible-only-with-factory-contradiction, unproven ranking and breadth are tested.

capstone.providers.factory:run_tool.judgment: Invalid arguments, a tool's own refusal, an over-long answer, a contract-breaking answer and any other failure are each reported as specified without leaking content.

capstone.providers.factory:SimulatorFact.judgment: Unknown tools cannot reach truth or approval; results carry tick and trace ids; the logger gets metadata only.

capstone.tools.observation:ObservationTo.judgment: Shape, range, unknown machine and the pressure-sensor refusal are tested, and the full-run leak test pins the key set of every tool's answer.
Eleven direct tests cover empty windows, single samples, mixed units, nonfinite values, factory sensors and the endpoint rate.
Size and shape are tested; idle readings are included by documented design.
gaps: No test pins bucket boundaries at the end of a range or a bucket larger than the range.

capstone.tools.actions:ApprovalDesk.carr.judgment: Refused until approved, once only, unknown ids refused, and an edited copy cannot unlock execution.

capstone.tools.actions:ActionTools.wait.judgment: Bounds, type checks and the clock moving are tested.

capstone.episode:run_episode.judgment: For the plumbing: a whole scripted episode is found, fixed, checked and scored; the same seed repeats; the agent's state never holds the answer key; the critic and settings reach the run.
gaps: The live model path (clients_for_jobs) is never executed offline; its reliability comes from the benchmark and master runs only.

capstone.experiment:record_of.judgment: Fields are shown to round-trip and older rows still read. By design the record keeps no evidence, hypotheses or tool arguments, so a saved master run cannot be judged for evidence quality without the separate audit log (audit finding R1).
gaps: Record completeness for post-hoc judging is a design gap, not a defect.

capstone.experiment:report.judgment: Lines and totals are tested; the summary line counts escalations on no-action cases as right recommendations (audit finding E2).

capstone.evals:report_of.judgment: Truth stays out of the policy, labels alone score accuracy, review-flagged labels stay unjudged, the critic fields and the abstention card are tested.
gaps: EvalCase carries no termination reason, so a timed-out run is indistinguishable from a reasoned one in the JSON report (audit finding R3).

capstone.evals:compare_reports.judgment: Same-scenario and unknown-accuracy rules are tested.
gaps: Configurations (step mode, critic, manual, models) are not compared, so two batches with different settings compare without a warning (audit finding X1).

capstone.evals:check_resume.judgment: Prefix matching is tested; settings are not compared (recorded in the EV1 walkthrough).
gaps: A resumed run can mix configurations (the 2026-10-30/31 run-2 files did).

capstone.evaluation.auto_label:propose.judgment: Thresholds and review marking are tested against a fake judgment client.
gaps: Agreement with hand labels has never been measured live (MVP_SCOPE 'finish the check on Jev's labels'); until then auto labels must not feed accuracy.

capstone.evaluation.labels:LabelBook.rea.judgment: Latest label wins; a missing file is empty.

capstone.learning:learn_from.judgment: Audit first, lesson only for a verified carried-out fix, code-written failure lesson, model failure costs only the lesson.

capstone.memory.policy:MemoryPromotionPo.judgment: Every refusal reason has a test, including hidden-truth text, memory-only and manual-only provenance, and no-action-taken.

capstone.providers.chat:FallbackClient.a.judgment: Time shares, retries with doubling pauses, non-transient failures moving on, invalid replies raising at once and the out-of-time flag are tested.

capstone.providers.chat:run_with_deadlin.judgment: Whole-request deadline, result and exception pass-through are tested.
gaps: The abandoned thread keeps running; documented, not tested for resource growth.

capstone.providers.hazards:UnreliablePro.judgment: Timeout, gap, stale record, blackout, recovery accounting and the untouched simulator are tested, and an episode with hazards repeats exactly.

capstone.providers.recall:RecallingProvi.judgment: Repeat refusal, the search allowance, store failures without detail and the memory source label are tested.

capstone.providers.manual:ManualProvider.judgment: As recall: limits, refusals, the manual source label; plus the leak check on sections.

capstone.manual.sections:check_no_leaks.judgment: Fault names, seeds, case ids and 'ground truth' are refused in any section.
gaps: A leak written in other words (a standard speed as a number) is guarded by a separate test only for job times and speeds.

capstone.simulator.simulator:Simulator.s.judgment: The order contract (reality, consequences, warming, readings, alarms) and determinism are pinned across the simulator test files.

capstone.simulator.simulator:Simulator.g.judgment: Immutable, order of scenarios, unchanged by the run, reading it changes nothing.

capstone.simulator.generator:build_scena.judgment: Seed determinism, forced faults and the untouched streams are tested; the known-answer cases pin thirteen factories.

capstone.simulator.challenge:build_chall.judgment: Composition, determinism and the pinned KA-09 truth.

capstone.agent.monitor:detect_anomaly.judgment: Executed only through episode and known-answer tests, which pin what it notices for thirteen cases and that it names no cause.
gaps: No direct test of the routine-check branch at max_ticks or of a stopped-machine status event being noticed before an alarm.

capstone.baseline:diagnose.judgment: Five tests and the known-case run; thresholds were tuned on seeds 1-20 and the held-out check is a printed table, not an assertion.
gaps: Its 9/9 on the known cases is on tuning-adjacent seeds; the agent comparison should use held-out seeds (HELD_OUT_SEEDS).

capstone.settings:Settings.blank_is_miss.judgment: Defaults, blank-is-missing, chains and the .env.example parity are tested.

capstone.tools.actions:ActionTools.propo.judgment: Unknown machine, unknown action, blank reason and hydraulics on a machine without them are refused and nothing is recorded; a good proposal is recorded pending with its tick and changes nothing in the factory.

capstone.tools.actions:ActionTools.execu.judgment: Malformed ids are refused; otherwise the desk's carry_out rules apply (approved only, once).

capstone.tools.actions:ActionTools.get_p.judgment: Read back after approval and rejection in the action-path tests; the copies it returns cannot be used to approve.
gaps: No direct test of the list's order or of a proposal carried out showing its executed and finish ticks.

capstone.tools.observation:ObservationTo.judgment: Past records then this run's, oldest first, with and without a machine filter; the stale-record hazard is tested on top of it.
gaps: Only 7 tests execute it; an unknown machine on this tool is checked through `_check` but not asserted here.
